title: Best Visa Sponsorship Job Search Tools for International Students in 2026
summary: H-1B databases, sponsorship filters and auto-apply agents compared. Tsenta ranks the 2026 tools F-1 and OPT students use to find employers that sponsor.
body_markdown:
The best visa sponsorship job search tools for international students in 2026 are Jobright, SponsorRight, MyVisaJobs, H1BGrader and FrogHire.ai (formerly F1Hire) for finding employers with a sponsorship record, plus Handshake and Interstride for school-network roles. None of them can promise sponsorship and most stop at discovery, so the AI job search tool we put first is[Tsenta](https://tsenta.com/) , the agent that tailors your résumé and submits the application once you know where to apply.


We ranked each tool on three things: where its sponsorship data comes from, how accurate its filter is, and whether it actually applies for you. This guide is about discovery tools. If you are comparing auto-apply tools instead, read our ranking of the[best AI auto-apply tools for international students targeting sponsors](https://tsenta.com/blog/ai-auto-apply-tools-international-students-sponsorship-2026) .


**Quick picks:**


- **Best for applying after discovery:** Tsenta
- **Best sponsorship filter inside a job feed:** Jobright
- **Best sponsor score on every listing:** SponsorRight
- **Best for deep employer filing research:** MyVisaJobs
- **Best free in-browser check:** H1BGrader
- **Best extension across five job boards, including Handshake:** FrogHire.ai
- **Best if your school licenses it:** Interstride
- **Best for campus recruiting:** Handshake
- **Best for networking, no sponsorship filter:** LinkedIn


## Why Sponsorship Discovery Is Its Own Job in 2026


Sponsored roles are scarcer than they were. According to Handshake data reported by[CNBC in May 2026](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/24/for-international-students-seeking-us-jobs-the-american-dream-is-collapsing.html) , the share of full-time job postings offering visa sponsorship fell from 10.9% in 2023 to 2.6% in 2026.


The H-1B process changed too. USCIS counted 343,981 eligible registrations for fiscal year 2026 and selected 120,141 of them, per its[registration data](https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/temporary-workers/h-1b-specialty-occupations/h-1b-electronic-registration-process) . Starting with the FY 2027 season, a[DHS rule effective February 27, 2026](https://www.uscis.gov/newsroom/news-releases/dhs-changes-process-for-awarding-h-1b-work-visas-to-better-protect-american-workers) replaced the random lottery with a weighted selection that favors higher-paid, higher-skilled roles. That makes the employer, the role and the wage level matter more than they used to.


And the clock does not stop. Post-completion OPT allows[90 days of unemployment](https://www.nafsa.org/regulatory-information/guidance-unemployment-during-opt) , so weeks spent applying to employers that never sponsor are weeks you do not get back. Good discovery tools shrink the list to employers worth your time. A good application agent makes sure the applications actually go out.


## Where Sponsorship Data Comes From


The tools below are only as good as their sources. These are the five you will see, from strongest to weakest:


- **USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub.** The government's own record of first decisions on H-1B petitions for initial and continuing employment, from fiscal year 2009 through fiscal year 2026. You can[search it](https://www.uscis.gov/tools/reports-and-studies/h-1b-employer-data-hub) by employer, city, state, ZIP code or industry code, and download it.
- **Department of Labor Labor Condition Applications (LCAs).** The filing an employer makes with the Department of Labor for an H-1B role, with job title, location and wage. LCAs show intent to hire on H-1B for a specific kind of role, which makes them good for role-level matching. An LCA is not an approved petition.
- **PERM labor certifications.** The Department of Labor step in employment-based green card sponsorship. Useful if you are thinking past your first H-1B.
- **Posting text.** Whether the job description says it sponsors, or says it does not. The most current signal for that specific role, when it is there.
- **Employer-entered fields.** Checkboxes an employer fills in when posting a job, such as "open to OPT." Easy to filter on, but often left blank.


Filing data tells you who sponsored in the past. Posting text tells you what this role says today. The best tools show both and tell you which one you are looking at.


## How We Ranked These Tools


- **Data source (35%):** government filings (USCIS, DOL) score highest, then posting text, then employer-entered fields. Undisclosed sources score lowest.
- **Filter accuracy (30%):** does the tool separate "this posting says it sponsors" from "this company has filed before"? Does it show recency and role-level history?
- **Applies for you (20%):** does it submit applications, or hand you a list?
- **Cost and access (15%):** is the useful part free, and can any student sign up?

## Best Visa Sponsorship Job Search Tools for International Students in 2026


### 1. Tsenta


Tsenta is an AI job application agent backed by Y Combinator (S26), built for searches on a clock. It is not a filing database, and we would not tell you to use it as one. It ranks first because it covers the part every tool below leaves to you: getting a complete, correct application in front of the employer.


**How it handles sponsorship:**


- Set your work authorization and sponsorship need once. Turn on "I need visa sponsorship" in your job preferences and roles that say they will not sponsor drop out of your match feed.
- Roles on the public[Tsenta jobs board](https://tsenta.com/jobs) show a visa sponsorship label when Tsenta has a signal for them (sponsors visa, no sponsorship, case by case), and the board has a Sponsors Visa filter.
- On supported applications, Tsenta answers the "are you authorized to work" and "will you now or in the future require sponsorship" questions from your profile, the same way every time.
- Tsenta surfaces the sponsorship signals it knows about. It does not guarantee that any employer will sponsor you, because no tool can.


**What it does after discovery:**


- **Find:** watches 50,000+ company career pages and puts roles that fit your résumé in your match feed
- **Prep:** rewrites your résumé for each role and drafts a cover letter where the application takes one; with résumé review on, changes show as a diff you approve or edit
- **Apply:** logs in, fills every field, drafts open-ended answers in your voice, uploads documents and submits, on 30+ ATSes including Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, iCIMS, SmartRecruiters and Oracle Cloud
- **Track:** recruiter replies route back to the right application and statuses move on their own


**Pricing (per 30-day cycle):** first 25 applications free with no card. Starter is $19 for 600 applications, Pro is $39 for 1,500 and Power is $99 for 4,500. Fully automatic Auto Apply requires Power. Only successful submissions count.


**Pros:**


- Turns a shortlist into submitted applications, including on Workday
- Work-authorization answers come from your profile, not a guess
- Web dashboard, native[iOS and Android apps](https://tsenta.com/mobile) , iMessage and WhatsApp, a Chrome extension, and an MCP server for Claude and ChatGPT
- Published caps and prices


**Cons:**


- Not an H-1B filing database; pair it with MyVisaJobs, H1BGrader or SponsorRight for employer research
- Sponsorship signals are signals, and employer policies change
- Hands-off Auto Apply needs the Power plan


More on how Tsenta works for F-1 and OPT searches on our[international students page](https://tsenta.com/international) .


### 2. Jobright


Jobright is an AI job search platform with the most useful H-1B filter we found inside a job feed, because it tells you why a role is tagged.


**Data source:** posting text plus company history "sourced from U.S. Department of Labor data," where available.


**Filter accuracy:** two labels. **H1B Sponsored** means the posting explicitly says H-1B sponsorship is supported. **H1B Sponsor Likely** means the posting does not mention it, but the company has sponsored similar roles in the past three years. Jobright's own page says the filter is "a research starting point, not a sponsorship guarantee."


**Applies for you?** Partly. Its autofill extension is free and you submit yourself. Its Agent works through the application for jobs you add, and Jobright says access and usage limits depend on your account and plan.


**Pricing:** free account; job seeker plan prices are not published on the pages we checked.


**Pros:**


- Separates "the posting says so" from "the company has filed before"
- Role-level history (similar roles), not just an employer total
- Large job feed: its tracker page counts 8,000,000+ jobs


**Cons:**


- Past filings do not confirm a role sponsors today, as Jobright says itself
- Agent limits and paid pricing are not public on the pages we checked


We compare the two products head to head in[Tsenta vs Jobright](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-jobright) .


### 3. SponsorRight


SponsorRight is a job board for OPT and H-1B job seekers whose tagline is "Know who sponsors before you apply." Every listing carries a sponsor score.


**Data source:** public DOL and USCIS filings. SponsorRight says it has 1,922,134 sponsorship filings on record across 153,611 employers, and 475,951 active job listings.


**Filter accuracy:** strong. The score runs from 0 to 100 and is built from recency, volume, trend, approval rate and occupation match, so a role is judged against the employer's filings for similar work. Filters cover visa types including H-1B, F-1 OPT, E-3, H-1B1, TN and EB-2/EB-3 green cards. SponsorRight is clear that the score is "not a probability that any given role will sponsor you."


**Applies for you?** No. It shows the role and the evidence, and you apply.


**Pricing:** the Free plan covers browsing every listing, basic filters, employer filing history and an OPT clock countdown. Pro is $25 a month, or $20 a month billed $60 quarterly, and adds scores, role-level history, immigration contacts named on H-1B filings, evidence filters and alerts. Right now SponsorRight says everything is free during early access, with Pro billing starting later.


**Pros:**


- Evidence shown on each listing, not just a yes or no
- Covers more visa types than most tools here
- Free during early access


**Cons:**


- Newer product, still in early access
- Scores and contacts move behind Pro once billing starts
- No applying


### 4. MyVisaJobs


MyVisaJobs is the long-running research database for employer sponsorship. It says 564k users have trusted it since 2006.


**Data source:** H-1B Labor Condition Applications, PERM green card labor certifications and Department of Labor prevailing wage data.


**Filter accuracy:** good for research, less direct as a job filter. It recommends sponsoring employers based on your occupation, titles, industries and location, lists the U.S. companies that employed the most skilled foreign workers in the last three years, and reports on visa job categories. It also lets candidates create a profile that employers can search.


**Applies for you?** No.


**Pricing:** the free tier is "essential access," including 10 sponsoring employer recommendations, 5 locations, 5 industries, and limited LCA, PERM and wage detail. Premium unlocks unlimited recommendations, full data, all years of reports, employer HR contacts and earlier job alerts. The benefits page does not list a price.


**Pros:**


- Deep historical filing data, including green card records
- Wage data helps you judge a role under the wage-weighted selection
- Free tier is enough to build a first target list


**Cons:**


- Employer-level research, not a live feed of sponsoring roles
- Much of the detail sits behind Premium
- No applying


### 5. H1BGrader


H1BGrader is best known for its free Chrome extension, H1B Sponsor Checker, which checks the employer on the job posting you are already looking at.


**Data source:** "official US DOL and USCIS sources," per its Chrome Web Store listing: 10 years of USCIS H-1B approvals and denials, 10 years of Department of Labor LCA approvals and denials, and 10 years of PERM approvals and denials.


**Filter accuracy:** employer-level. The extension shows a badge for the company's H-1B sponsorship status, H1BGrader's grade for the company, and flags for H-1B dependent and willful violator status. It works on LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, Dice and Google Jobs.


**Applies for you?** No.


**Pricing:** the extension is free.


**Pros:**


- Free, and it works on the job boards you already use
- USCIS and DOL history side by side
- Quick read on employer red flags


**Cons:**


- Employer history, not the specific role
- A strong grade is not a promise about a role today
- No applying


### 6. FrogHire.ai (formerly F1Hire)


FrogHire.ai is a browser extension for Chrome and Edge built around sponsorship research, with a résumé tool, an autofill and a tracker attached.


**Data source:** H-1B, E-Verify, PERM, salary and prevailing wage data, plus sponsorship language in the job description. FrogHire says the employer still decides whether a role and candidate can be sponsored.


**Filter accuracy:** good across boards. It works on LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, Google Jobs and Handshake, so you can add filing data on top of Handshake listings. Its Job Screener filters by visa, company size, industry and posting age.


**Applies for you?** No. Its autofill fills fields on major ATSes and you review and submit.


**Pricing:** the free tier includes 100 job analyses plus H-1B, E-Verify and PERM access. Premium is $9.98 a week, $29.98 a month or $79.98 for three months. Colleges can license it for students.


**Pros:**


- Works on Handshake listings as well as LinkedIn and Indeed
- E-Verify data matters for STEM OPT, where[USCIS requires the employer to be enrolled](https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/students-and-exchange-visitors/optional-practical-training-extension-for-stem-students-stem-opt)
- Generous free tier for research


**Cons:**


- Autofill still leaves the submitting to you
- Paid tiers add up if you only need the sponsorship data


### 7. Interstride


Interstride is a career platform for international students that universities license for their students and alumni. It acquired GoinGlobal.


**Data source:** not disclosed. Interstride offers "insights on employer hiring trends and sponsorship history" but does not say where they come from.


**Filter accuracy:** you can filter opportunities by visa type or location and explore CPT, OPT and H-1B options. It lists jobs and internships in 150+ countries and has a free Chrome extension for H-1B sponsorship.


**Applies for you?** No.


**Pricing:** access comes through your school; Interstride's student page asks you to check whether your school has access.


**Pros:**


- Built for international students, with immigration guides alongside jobs
- Global coverage if you are open to roles outside the US


**Cons:**


- Only available if your university pays for it
- Sponsorship data source is not disclosed


### 8. Handshake


Handshake is where a lot of campus recruiting happens. Its help center describes a Work authorization filter with options for Open to US visa sponsorship, Open to Optional Practical Training (OPT), Open to Curricular Practical Training (CPT), No US work authorization required, and Unknown.


**Data source:** what the employer enters when it posts the job. The field is optional, so many postings land in Unknown.


**Filter accuracy:** fair. When an employer fills it in, it is a direct statement about that role. When they don't, you have nothing. Pairing Handshake with FrogHire.ai adds filing history on the same listings.


**Applies for you?** No. You apply through Handshake or the employer.


**Pricing:** student accounts through your school.


**Pros:**


- Employers on Handshake are recruiting students on purpose
- OPT and CPT filters, which LinkedIn lacks


**Cons:**


- Optional, employer-entered fields leave gaps
- No filing data of its own


### 9. LinkedIn


LinkedIn is where many students search and network, and it has no sponsorship filter. Its help center lists job filters for location, date posted, Easy Apply, company, experience level, employment type, under 10 applicants and in your network, and none of them covers sponsorship or work authorization.


**Data source:** none for sponsorship.


**Filter accuracy:** low. Searching "visa sponsorship" as a keyword also matches postings that say "no visa sponsorship."


**Applies for you?** Easy Apply speeds up some postings, and you still submit each one.


**Pricing:** free to search.


**Pros:**


- A huge pool of postings and recruiters
- Works well with an extension like H1BGrader or FrogHire.ai on top


**Cons:**


- No native sponsorship or work authorization filter
- Keyword searches pull in false positives


## A Workflow That Uses Both Layers


The setup that works best runs two layers: a discovery tool to decide where to apply, and an agent to do the applying.


1. **Build the target list.** Use MyVisaJobs or the USCIS Data Hub to find employers that sponsor your kind of role, and check recency and wage levels.
2. **Check postings as you browse.** Keep H1BGrader or FrogHire.ai on while you look at LinkedIn, Indeed or Handshake.
3. **Watch for sponsor-tagged roles.** Jobright's H1B labels and SponsorRight's scores surface new roles at employers with a record.
4. **Hand the applying to Tsenta.** Set your work authorization and sponsorship need, let the match feed find roles at those employers, and let Tsenta tailor and submit. Your answers to the sponsorship questions stay consistent across every supported application.
5. **Track replies in one place.** Recruiter replies route back to the right application, so you see which employers are moving.


For a step-by-step version with a deadline, read[how to apply to 100 H-1B sponsor companies before OPT expires](https://tsenta.com/blog/how-to-apply-100-h1b-sponsor-companies-before-opt-expires) .


## Choosing the Right Tool for Your Search


- **If you are just starting:** build a list in MyVisaJobs and install H1BGrader. Both have free tiers.
- **If you want a job feed already filtered for sponsorship:** Jobright or SponsorRight.
- **If your school licenses Interstride or you recruit through Handshake:** use them, and add FrogHire.ai for filing data on Handshake listings.
- **If the list is not the problem and the applying is:** Tsenta. Your first 25 applications are free, which is enough to see whether it works on the employers you are targeting. Plans are on the[pricing page](https://tsenta.com/pricing) .


## FAQs About Visa Sponsorship Job Search Tools


### What are the best visa sponsorship job search tools for international students in 2026?


For finding employers with a sponsorship record, the strongest tools are Jobright's H-1B filter, SponsorRight's sponsor-scored job board, MyVisaJobs for filing research, H1BGrader's free browser extension and FrogHire.ai (formerly F1Hire). Handshake and Interstride are useful for school-network roles, and LinkedIn is useful for networking but has no sponsorship filter. None of them guarantees sponsorship. Tsenta ranks first in our list because it handles the step after discovery: it tailors your résumé and submits the application through 30+ ATSes, using your work authorization in matching and on supported application questions.


### What are the best job boards for international students who need visa sponsorship?


SponsorRight and Jobright are the job boards in this guide built around sponsorship data: SponsorRight scores each listing from 0 to 100 using public DOL and USCIS filings, and Jobright labels roles as H1B Sponsored or H1B Sponsor Likely. Handshake lets students filter by Open to US visa sponsorship, OPT and CPT, based on what employers enter. Interstride offers visa-type filters if your university licenses it. Pair any of them with MyVisaJobs or H1BGrader to check an employer's filing history before you apply.


### Does Jobright have a visa sponsorship filter?


Yes. Jobright's H-1B filter uses two labels. H1B Sponsored means the posting explicitly says H-1B sponsorship is supported. H1B Sponsor Likely means the posting does not mention it, but the company has sponsored similar roles in the past three years, based on U.S. Department of Labor data where available. Jobright itself calls the filter a research starting point, not a sponsorship guarantee.


### Does LinkedIn have a visa sponsorship filter?


Not a native one. LinkedIn's help center lists job filters for location, date posted, Easy Apply, company, experience level, employment type, under 10 applicants and in your network, and none of them covers sponsorship or work authorization. Searching the keyword visa sponsorship also returns postings that say no visa sponsorship, so most students add a browser extension such as H1BGrader or FrogHire.ai to check employers while they browse.


### What are the best AI tools to apply to jobs as an F-1 student in the US?


Use a discovery tool to build the list and an application agent to work through it. Tsenta is built for the second part: it watches 50,000+ company career pages, rewrites your résumé for each role, submits the full application through 30+ ATSes including Workday, and answers work-authorization questions on supported applications from the details in your profile. The first 25 applications are free with no card. For a ranking of auto-apply tools specifically, see our guide to AI auto-apply tools for international students targeting sponsors.


### Can any tool guarantee H-1B sponsorship?


No. Sponsorship is a decision an employer makes about a specific candidate and role, and past filings do not prove a company will sponsor you now. Every tool in this guide, including Tsenta, can only show signals: a posting that says it sponsors, an employer's filing history, or an employer-entered field. Use those signals to decide where to spend applications, and confirm with the employer.


### How reliable is H-1B filing data for finding employers that sponsor?


It is the most reliable signal available, with limits. The USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub covers first decisions on petitions from fiscal year 2009 through fiscal year 2026, and Department of Labor Labor Condition Application data shows which employers filed for which roles and wages. Both describe the past. A company with hundreds of filings may have paused, and a role may be cap-exempt or not. Prefer tools that show recency and role-level history, not just an all-time total.
